library(nlmixr2lib)

# Models and source

Lakshminarayana 2015 studies the spiroindolone class of PfATP4 inhibitors in the
*Plasmodium berghei* 4-day suppressive mouse model. It reports three kinds of
separately fitted model, packaged here as eleven model files that share this
vignette:

| Model file | What it is | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_mouse` | Naive-pooled two-compartment oral PK of cipargamin (KAE609) in NMRI mice, Michaelis-Menten elimination | Table 4, equation 2 |
| `Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_cmaxtre` | Sigmoid model of day-4 parasitemia on Cmax/TRE | Table 5, Cmax/TRE column |
| `Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_auctre` | Sigmoid model of day-4 parasitemia on AUC0-48/TRE | Table 5, AUC0-48/TRE column |
| `Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_ttre` | Sigmoid model of day-4 parasitemia on %T>TRE | Table 5, %T>TRE column |
| `Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_doseresponse` | Single-dose dose-response of cipargamin, compound (+)-7 | Table 3 |
| `Lakshminarayana_2015_spiroindolone1_doseresponse` ... `spiroindolone6_doseresponse` | Single-dose dose-response of analogs (+)-1 to (+)-6 | Table 3 |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_mouse"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.03274-14> (PMCID: PMC4335872, open access)

The threshold TRE is twice the ex vivo *P. berghei* IC99 of cipargamin:
IC99 = 61.6 nM, so TRE = 123 nM = 48 ng/mL (Results, 'KAE609 exhibits
time-dependent killing'). The Cmax and AUC models carry TRE as the fixed
parameter `tre` and take the absolute exposure as a covariate; the %T>TRE model
takes the already-formed percentage.

```{r descriptions, results = "asis"}
mods <- c(
  "Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_mouse",
  "Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_cmaxtre",
  "Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_auctre",
  "Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_ttre",
  "Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_doseresponse"
)
for (m in mods) {
  cat("**`", m, "`** -- ", rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))$description, "\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

# Population

**PK.** Female specific-pathogen-free NMRI mice (Janvier, France), infected
(24 h after intravenous inoculation with 2 x 10^7 *P. berghei* GFP ANKA
parasitized erythrocytes) and uninfected, each given a single oral dose of
5.3 mg/kg cipargamin in 10% ethanol / 30% PEG 400 / 60% (10% vitamin E TPGS).
Plasma was sampled destructively at 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 24 and 48 h
(Figure 2 shows about three mice per time per group). Table 4 shows no
difference in PK between infected and uninfected animals, so the data were
pooled and fitted without between-animal variability. NMRI exposure was about
4-fold higher than in CD-1 mice at a comparable dose (Tables 2 and 4), which is
why the efficacy strain was used for the PK model.

**Efficacy.** Female NMRI mice (20-22 g), infected as above on day 0, treated
orally from 24 h post-infection, with parasitemia (parasitized erythrocytes per
100 erythrocytes) read by flow cytometry at 72 h post-infection. The
dose-response studies used single doses of 2.5, 5, 10, 30 and 100 mg/kg in
groups of five (plus 0.5-200 mg/kg for cipargamin, Figure 1). The cipargamin
dose-fractionation study used total daily doses of 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8 mg/kg
given once, as two doses 12 h apart or as three doses 8 h apart, four mice per
regimen (Table 1); vehicle controls averaged 35.51% +/- 3.86% parasitemia.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_auctre")()$population, max.level = 1, width = 78)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| PK: `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | Methods, 'Pharmacokinetic modeling and simulation for KAE609': two-compartment model, first-order absorption, nonlinear elimination |
| PK: `cl = vmax / (km + Cp)` | n/a | Equation 2 |
| `lka` | 1.78 1/h | Table 4 |
| `lvc` | 4.4 L/kg | Table 4 |
| `lvp` | 5.1 L/kg | Table 4 |
| `lq` | 0.61 L/h/kg | Table 4 |
| `lvmax` | 143 ug/h/kg | Table 4 |
| `lkm` | 34.1 ug/L | Table 4 |
| PK `propSd` | 0 (FIXED) | Not reported (naive-pooled fit) |
| Index and dose models: `log10 P = log10 Pmin + (log10 Pmax - log10 Pmin) / (1 + 10^((log10 EZ50 - log10 x) * s))` | n/a | Equation 1; x untransformed for %T>TRE (Methods, 'PK-PD relationship analysis of KAE609') |
| `tre` | 0.048 ug/mL (FIXED) | Results: IC99 61.6 nM; 2 x IC99 = 123 nM or 48 ng/mL |
| Cmax/TRE: `lpmin`, `lpmax`, `lec50`, `hill` | 0.12, 34.51, 5.43, -1.87 | Table 5 |
| AUC0-48/TRE: `lpmin`, `lpmax`, `lec50`, `hill` | 0.13, 32.66, 52.72, -1.63 | Table 5 |
| %T>TRE: `lpmin`, `lpmax`, `lec50`, `hill` | 0.15, 53.09, 32.06, -0.031 | Table 5 |
| Index-model `expSd` | 0.34, 0.22, 0.17 x ln(10) | Results: standard error of the estimate Sy.x (log10 units) |
| Dose models: `lpmin`, `lpmax`, `led90`, `hill` | per compound | Table 3 |
| Dose models: `ez50 = ed90 / 9^(1 / -hill)` | n/a | Derived; see 'ED90 and EZ50' below |
| Dose-model `expSd` | 0 (FIXED) | Not reported |

# Cipargamin PK model

```{r pk-sim}
pk <- readModelDb("Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_mouse")
pk_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.01), seq(4, 96, by = 0.1))))
pk_events <- rxode2::et(amt = 5.3, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(pk_grid, cmt = "central") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(treatment = "5.3 mg/kg")
pk_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(pk, pk_events, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(pk_sim$Cc))
```

```{r figure-2a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2A of Lakshminarayana 2015: typical cipargamin plasma concentration after a single 5.3 mg/kg oral dose in NMRI mice (linear scale)."}
pk_plot <- pk_sim |>
  filter(time <= 48) |>
  mutate(conc_ngml = 1000 * Cc)
ggplot(pk_plot, aes(time, conc_ngml)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Cipargamin (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 2A of Lakshminarayana 2015.") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r figure-2b, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2B of Lakshminarayana 2015 (semi-log scale); the dashed line is TRE = 48 ng/mL."}
ggplot(pk_plot |> filter(conc_ngml > 1), aes(time, conc_ngml)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 48, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Cipargamin (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 2B of Lakshminarayana 2015.") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The Figure 2 model line peaks at about 950 ng/mL near 1.5 h and falls to
about 8 ng/mL at 48 h. The packaged model reproduces both:

```{r pk-gates}
pk_cmax <- max(pk_sim$Cc)
pk_tmax <- pk_sim$time[which.max(pk_sim$Cc)]
pk_c48 <- 1000 * pk_sim$Cc[pk_sim$time == 48]
c(cmax_ngml = 1000 * pk_cmax, tmax_h = pk_tmax, c48_ngml = pk_c48)
stopifnot(
  pk_cmax > 0.90, pk_cmax < 1.00,
  pk_tmax > 1, pk_tmax < 2,
  pk_c48 > 4, pk_c48 < 16
)
```

## PKNCA against Table 4

Table 4 reports the noncompartmental Cmax and AUC0-inf of the observed mean
profiles. The model is a fit to those same data, so it should land close to
them but not on them.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- pk_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(id = 1L) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 5.3, treatment = "5.3 mg/kg"),
  amt ~ time | treatment + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,  ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs,
  "5.3 mg/kg", 1.01,  13.21
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", aucinf.obs = "ug*h/mL", tmax = "h", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Typical-value PKNCA vs. Table 4 (uninfected NMRI mice). * differs by >20%.")
```

The infected group's NCA values (Cmax 0.96 ug/mL, AUC0-inf 12.64 ug*h/mL) are
within 5% of the uninfected ones. The simulated values are 5-10% below the
uninfected NCA, the expected size of the gap between a naive-pooled model fit
and the trapezoidal NCA of the noisy mean profile.

## Table 1: PK-PD indices of the dose-fractionation regimens

The authors used this model in Berkeley Madonna to simulate Cmax, AUC0-48 and
%T>TRE for each of the 15 regimens of Table 1. Simulating the same regimens --
all doses given on the first treatment day, then no further dosing until the
48 h readout -- reproduces every tabulated index:

```{r table-1}
tre <- 0.048
table1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~total, ~n_doses, ~cmax_tre, ~auc_tre, ~ttre, ~par_mean, ~par_sd,
  8,   1, 29.95, 513.68, 99.9,  0.15, 0.03,
  8,   2, 19.40, 414.93, 99.8,  0.18, 0.04,
  8,   3, 16.44, 383.23, 99.8,  0.16, 0.02,
  4,   1, 14.56, 148.45, 54.5,  0.63, 0.57,
  4,   2,  7.92, 106.02, 56.1,  0.43, 0.38,
  4,   3,  6.00,  92.12, 57.3,  0.55, 0.28,
  2,   1,  6.93,  45.07, 23.0,  5.64, 1.69,
  2,   2,  3.37,  30.66, 22.7,  6.48, 3.94,
  2,   3,  2.24,  25.18, 22.3, 10.83, 4.67,
  1,   1,  3.21,  14.57, 10.7, 17.82, 3.05,
  1,   2,  1.49,  10.16,  8.8, 18.19, 6.81,
  1,   3,  0.96,   8.55,  0.0, 20.31, 5.71,
  0.5, 1,  1.45,   4.98,  4.3, 28.82, 4.49,
  0.5, 2,  0.67,   3.75,  0.0, 38.28, 2.95,
  0.5, 3,  0.43,   3.34,  0.0, 35.37, 5.32
) |>
  mutate(regimen = paste0(total, " mg/kg x", n_doses))

idx_grid <- seq(0, 48, by = 0.005)
sim_indices <- function(total, n_doses) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = total / n_doses, cmt = "depot",
                   ii = if (n_doses > 1) 24 / n_doses else 0,
                   addl = n_doses - 1) |>
    rxode2::et(idx_grid, cmt = "central")
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(pk, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == length(idx_grid))
  auc <- sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2)
  tibble(CMAX = max(s$Cc), AUC_CIPARGAMIN = auc,
         FTTRE_CIPARGAMIN = 100 * mean(s$Cc > tre))
}
table1 <- bind_cols(table1, bind_rows(Map(sim_indices, table1$total, table1$n_doses))) |>
  mutate(
    cmax_pct = 100 * (CMAX / tre / cmax_tre - 1),
    auc_pct = 100 * (AUC_CIPARGAMIN / tre / auc_tre - 1),
    ttre_diff = FTTRE_CIPARGAMIN - ttre
  )

table1 |>
  transmute(regimen,
            "Cmax/TRE (paper)" = cmax_tre, "Cmax/TRE (model)" = round(CMAX / tre, 2),
            "AUC0-48/TRE (paper)" = auc_tre, "AUC0-48/TRE (model)" = round(AUC_CIPARGAMIN / tre, 2),
            "%T>TRE (paper)" = ttre, "%T>TRE (model)" = round(FTTRE_CIPARGAMIN, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table 1 PK-PD indices: published vs. the packaged PK model.")

# Same model, same regimens, no random effects: the only differences are the
# rounding of the printed values (two decimals on indices as small as 0.43)
# and the integration grid.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(table1$cmax_pct)) < 1,
  max(abs(table1$auc_pct)) < 1,
  max(abs(table1$ttre_diff)) < 0.5
)
```

This also pins the dosing design: a two-day course (doses repeated on the
second treatment day) would roughly double every AUC0-48/TRE value.

# PK-PD index models

Each index model takes one exposure column. The simulated indices from the
previous section feed all three, alongside a vehicle record with every exposure
set to 0.

```{r index-solve}
mod_cmax <- readModelDb("Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_cmaxtre")
mod_auc <- readModelDb("Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_auctre")
mod_ttre <- readModelDb("Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_ttre")

# The index models have no time dependence, so each exposure value is one
# observation row of a single subject (a time-varying covariate); this avoids
# rxode2's multi-subject-without-omega warning.
solve_index <- function(mod, cov_name, values) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq_along(values), evid = 0, amt = NA_real_)
  ev[[cov_name]] <- values
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  stopifnot(nrow(out) == length(values), !anyNA(out$parasites))
  out$parasites
}

table1 <- table1 |>
  mutate(
    pred_cmax = solve_index(mod_cmax, "CMAX", CMAX),
    pred_auc = solve_index(mod_auc, "AUC_CIPARGAMIN", AUC_CIPARGAMIN),
    pred_ttre = solve_index(mod_ttre, "FTTRE_CIPARGAMIN", FTTRE_CIPARGAMIN)
  )
vehicle <- c(
  cmax = solve_index(mod_cmax, "CMAX", 0),
  auc = solve_index(mod_auc, "AUC_CIPARGAMIN", 0),
  ttre = solve_index(mod_ttre, "FTTRE_CIPARGAMIN", 0)
)
vehicle
```

At zero exposure the Cmax and AUC models return their Pmax (34.51% and
32.66%), close to the observed vehicle mean of 35.51%. The %T>TRE model enters
its index untransformed, so at 0% it has not yet reached its fitted upper
asymptote (53.09%): it predicts about 31%, which is what Figure 3C shows at the
left edge (log10 parasitemia about 1.5).

```{r figure-3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Lakshminarayana 2015: day-4 parasitemia against each PK-PD index. Points are the Table 1 regimen means (+/- SD); lines are the packaged models.", fig.height = 3.6}
curve_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(panel = "A: Cmax/TRE", x = 10^seq(log10(0.3), log10(50), length.out = 200)) |>
    mutate(y = solve_index(mod_cmax, "CMAX", x * tre)),
  tibble(panel = "B: AUC0-48/TRE", x = 10^seq(log10(2), log10(700), length.out = 200)) |>
    mutate(y = solve_index(mod_auc, "AUC_CIPARGAMIN", x * tre)),
  tibble(panel = "C: %T>TRE", x = seq(0, 100, length.out = 200)) |>
    mutate(y = solve_index(mod_ttre, "FTTRE_CIPARGAMIN", x))
)
point_df <- bind_rows(
  table1 |> transmute(panel = "A: Cmax/TRE", x = cmax_tre, par_mean, par_sd),
  table1 |> transmute(panel = "B: AUC0-48/TRE", x = auc_tre, par_mean, par_sd),
  table1 |> transmute(panel = "C: %T>TRE", x = ttre, par_mean, par_sd)
) |>
  mutate(lo = log10(pmax(par_mean - par_sd, 0.05)), hi = log10(par_mean + par_sd))

# As in the paper, panels A and B use a log10 index axis and panel C a linear
# one. Regimens with %T>TRE = 0 have positive Cmax and AUC, so no point is lost.
to_axis <- function(panel, x) ifelse(panel == "C: %T>TRE", x, log10(x))
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = curve_df, aes(to_axis(panel, x), log10(y))) +
  geom_pointrange(data = point_df,
                  aes(to_axis(panel, x), log10(par_mean), ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                  shape = 21, size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "log10 index (A, B); percent of 48 h (C)", y = "log10 [% parasitemia]",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Lakshminarayana 2015.") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r index-gates}
fit_stats <- table1 |>
  summarise(across(c(pred_cmax, pred_auc, pred_ttre),
                   ~ sqrt(mean((log10(.x) - log10(par_mean))^2))))
knitr::kable(fit_stats, digits = 3,
             caption = "Root-mean-square log10 error of each model against the 15 Table 1 regimen means.")

ec50_cmax <- exp(rxode2::rxode(mod_cmax)$iniDf |> filter(name == "lec50") |> pull(est))
stopifnot(
  # Discussion: the Cmax producing half the maximal effect in vivo is 260 ng/mL,
  # i.e. EC50 (5.43) x TRE (48 ng/mL).
  abs(1000 * ec50_cmax * tre - 260) < 3,
  # The fits are ranked by the paper as %T>TRE best and Cmax/TRE worst (R^2
  # 0.97, 0.95, 0.88). Deterministic predictions, so a structural error (a
  # wrong scale on the index, a missing log10) shows up as an error of a
  # log unit or more; the observed RMS errors are 0.1-0.3.
  fit_stats$pred_cmax < 0.5,
  fit_stats$pred_auc < 0.4,
  fit_stats$pred_ttre < 0.4,
  abs(vehicle[["cmax"]] - 34.51) < 0.1,
  abs(vehicle[["auc"]] - 32.66) < 0.1
)
```

# Dose-response models (Table 3)

## ED90 and EZ50

Table 3 reports ED90 rather than the EZ50 of equation 1. Two readings of ED90
are possible: the dose giving 90% of the maximal reduction on the fitted
(log10) scale, or the dose reducing parasitemia to 10% of Pmax. The packaged
models use the first, `EZ50 = ED90 / 9^(1 / |s|)`. Two checks support it.
First, the midpoints of the Figure 1 curves sit at the derived EZ50 (for
cipargamin about 2.5 mg/kg, log10 dose 0.4; for (+)-5 about 18 mg/kg, log10
dose 1.26), whereas the second reading would put the cipargamin midpoint near
5.5 mg/kg. Second, the Results quote 50%, 90% and 99% reductions in
parasitemia for cipargamin at 1.2, 2.7 and 5.3 mg/kg from an earlier study;
the first reading gives about 43%, 93% and 98.5% (computed below), and the
second only about 45% at 2.7 mg/kg.

```{r dose-models}
dose_models <- c(
  "(+)-1" = "Lakshminarayana_2015_spiroindolone1_doseresponse",
  "(+)-2" = "Lakshminarayana_2015_spiroindolone2_doseresponse",
  "(+)-3" = "Lakshminarayana_2015_spiroindolone3_doseresponse",
  "(+)-4" = "Lakshminarayana_2015_spiroindolone4_doseresponse",
  "(+)-5" = "Lakshminarayana_2015_spiroindolone5_doseresponse",
  "(+)-6" = "Lakshminarayana_2015_spiroindolone6_doseresponse",
  "(+)-7 (KAE609)" = "Lakshminarayana_2015_cipargamin_doseresponse"
)
solve_dose <- function(model_name, doses) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq_along(doses), evid = 0, amt = NA_real_, DOSE = doses)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(model_name), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  stopifnot(nrow(out) == length(doses), !anyNA(out$parasites))
  out
}
dose_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(dose_models), function(cmpd) {
  ini <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(dose_models[[cmpd]]))$iniDf
  p <- setNames(ini$est, ini$name)
  ed90 <- exp(p[["led90"]])
  out <- solve_dose(dose_models[[cmpd]], c(0, ed90, 1e4))
  lo <- log10(exp(p[["lpmin"]])); hi <- log10(exp(p[["lpmax"]]))
  tibble(
    compound = cmpd, ED90 = ed90, hill = p[["hill"]],
    EZ50 = ed90 / 9^(1 / -p[["hill"]]),
    P_at_0 = out$parasites[1], P_at_ED90 = out$parasites[2],
    frac_max_log_reduction = (hi - log10(out$parasites[2])) / (hi - lo)
  )
}))
knitr::kable(dose_summary, digits = c(0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3),
             caption = "Table 3 models: derived EZ50 and the predicted parasitemia at ED90.")

kae <- solve_dose(dose_models[["(+)-7 (KAE609)"]], c(0, 1.2, 2.7, 5.3))
kae_red <- 100 * (1 - kae$parasites[-1] / kae$parasites[1])
names(kae_red) <- c("1.2 mg/kg", "2.7 mg/kg", "5.3 mg/kg")
kae_red

stopifnot(
  all(abs(dose_summary$frac_max_log_reduction - 0.9) < 1e-6),
  # The earlier study's ED90 of 2.7 mg/kg: about 93% under the log10-scale
  # reading of ED90, about 45% under the 10%-of-Pmax reading.
  kae_red[["2.7 mg/kg"]] > 85, kae_red[["2.7 mg/kg"]] < 97,
  kae_red[["5.3 mg/kg"]] > 96
)
```

```{r figure-1, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1 of Lakshminarayana 2015: log10 day-4 parasitemia against log10 single oral dose for each spiroindolone. Vehicle (dose 0) is drawn at log10 dose -1, as in the paper.", fig.height = 5}
log_dose <- seq(-1, 2.4, by = 0.02)
fig1 <- bind_rows(lapply(names(dose_models), function(cmpd) {
  out <- solve_dose(dose_models[[cmpd]], 10^log_dose)
  tibble(compound = cmpd, log_dose = log_dose, log_par = log10(out$parasites))
}))
ggplot(fig1, aes(log_dose, log_par)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~compound, ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "log10 dose (mg/kg)", y = "log10 [% parasitemia]",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Lakshminarayana 2015 (model lines only; the individual animal data are not published).") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Dose-fractionation design.** Table 1 describes the regimens as a total daily
  dose given once, twice or three times "over 24 h". The packaged validation
  gives all doses on the first treatment day only; this reproduces every Table 1
  index, and repeating the doses on a second day does not.
- **ED90 reading.** Table 3 prints ED90 but not EZ50. The models derive
  `EZ50 = ED90 / 9^(1 / |s|)` (ED90 = 90% of the maximal reduction on the
  log10 scale); see 'ED90 and EZ50' above for the two checks that settle it.
- **Residual error.** The index models use the reported standard error of the
  estimate Sy.x (0.34, 0.22 and 0.17 log10 units) as a log-normal SD, converted
  to the natural-log scale by multiplying by ln(10). The PK model (naive pooled)
  and the Table 3 NONMEM dose-response fits report no residual or between-animal
  variability, so those are held at 0.
- **Bioavailability.** The authors assumed 100% oral bioavailability in NMRI
  mice because no intravenous NMRI data were collected (Discussion); Vc, Vp, Q
  and Vmax are therefore apparent (divided by F) values.
- **Michaelis-Menten units.** Table 4 gives Vmax in ug/h/kg and Km in ug/L.
  The model compares Km against `1000 * Cc` (ug/L) so that equation 2 returns a
  clearance in L/h/kg.
- **%T>TRE at zero exposure.** The %T>TRE model enters the index
  untransformed, as the Methods state, so it predicts about 31% rather than the
  fitted Pmax (53.09%) for a vehicle-treated animal; Figure 3C shows the same.
- **Total concentrations.** All indices use total plasma concentrations
  (plasma protein binding about 99.8% in mice, supplementary Table S1).
- **Models not packaged.** Table 2 (CD-1 mouse PK and in vitro potency of the
  analogs) is noncompartmental analysis only and has no model to package.
  (-)-6 and (-)-7 had no efficacy and no dose-response fit.
- **Number of animals.** Neither the PK study nor the pooled dose-response
  studies state the number of animals, so `n_subjects` is left `NA` for those
  models.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC as
  of 2026-11-25.
